item.title: Adding dependencies to your Node.js native addons using Conan
item.description:
This is an old article and is no longer maintained. It uses Conan 1, and its workflow and commands have not been updated for Conan 2.

We have already covered how to write a simple C++ hello world native addon in a previous post. Now, we are going to add dependencies to that simple example, manage them with Conan and run the code in Node.js.

If you are not familiar with Conan, please check the getting started in the documentation.

item.title: Creating C++ Node Addons using N-API
item.description:
This is an old article and is no longer maintained. It reflects the Node.js toolchain available in 2020, so current versions may use different APIs or commands.

With Node.js addons we can load our C++ libraries as if they were ordinary Node.js modules. The recommended way to implement these addons is using the N-API. N-API has been part of the Node.js distribution since v8 and became stable in v10.
